labels.text: Work: multi-step tasks with tools, files, and reviewable deliverables

S60.01.needs: a paid account (Pro or above), a project to select
S60.01.note: The Work segment is only rendered when the project picker is present and the plan allows Work.
steps: Sign in on a paid plan (Free trial is excluded) and open a chat with a project selected so the project picker shows.
In the composer, click the segment labelled Work next to Chat.
Type a goal in the composer and send it.
Look for a task that starts as a Work run (a plan review or activity appears), not a plain chat reply. Compare with Expected.
S60.01.where: Chat composer > Chat | Work switch > Work (Work tools palette appears under the Add attachments and tools button)

S60.02.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one task
S60.02.note: No rename control was found on the Tasks page; the row title is the source chat's conversation title (runTitle in TasksPage.tsx), so changing it is done in the source chat, which I did not verify.
steps: Sign in and click Chats and tasks in the sidebar.
Choose the Tasks filter.
Read the title on each task row.
Open a task and click Open source chat; compare the title shown there with the row title.
S60.02.where: Sidebar > Chats and tasks > Tasks filter > select a task row (title shown on the row)

S60.03.needs: a task that was started with a goal
steps: Press Cmd+K and choose Work history.
Click a task row.
Read the Goal block at the top of the task details.
Compare the goal text with what you typed when starting the task.
S60.03.where: Command palette (Cmd+K) > Work history > open a task > Goal section

S60.04.needs: a paid account, a project selected
S60.04.note: The Deliverable value is sent with the goal; the task detail panel does not show it as its own labelled field, so check it in the Goal text.
steps: In a Work composer, click the + button labelled Add attachments and tools.
Click Add scope (optional).
Type in the Deliverable field, for example a report or a file.
Send the goal and open the task; check that the deliverable appears in the task details.
S60.04.where: Composer > Add attachments and tools (+) > Add scope (optional) > Deliverable

S60.05.needs: a paid account, connected apps or folders for the sections to fill
steps: In a Work composer, click Add attachments and tools (+).
Read the Work tools palette.
Look at the sections Connected apps, Folders, Skills and Plugins and tick the ones the task may use.
Compare the ticked sources with the sources shown in the task after it starts.
S60.05.where: Composer > Add attachments and tools (+) > Work tools palette > Connected apps, Folders, Skills, Plugins

S60.06.note: Only two tool choices have translated labels in the en file; the source code may list more.
steps: In a Work composer, click Add attachments and tools (+) and then Add scope (optional).
Read the Tools this task may use group.
Tick or untick Web search and browsing and Code execution.
Send the goal and check the task only uses the ticked tools.
S60.06.where: Composer > Add attachments and tools (+) > Add scope (optional) > Tools this task may use

S60.08.note: The footer model selector is hidden in image and video modes.
steps: In a Chat or Work composer, look at the composer footer.
Click the model name button (its accessible name ends with Change model).
Pick another model and close the list.
Send a Work goal and open the task; check the model is shown on the task row.
S60.08.where: Composer footer > model button (aria label Change model)

S60.09.needs: a model that supports reasoning effort
S60.09.note: The effort control only appears when the selected model has an effort setting.
steps: In the composer footer, click the button titled Reasoning effort.
Move the Reasoning effort slider to another level.
Send the goal.
Check the level on the task after it starts; compare with Expected.
S60.09.where: Composer footer > Reasoning effort button > Reasoning effort slider

S60.13.needs: a paid account, a project selected, the agent must produce a plan
steps: Send a Work goal in a project chat.
Wait for the Review the plan card to appear.
Edit a step text, or click Add a step or Remove this step.
Click Start work, or Cancel, and compare with Expected.
S60.13.where: Work chat > send a goal > Review the plan card (Start work or Cancel)

S60.14.note: Step status is shown only by coloured dots, with no status word, so a tester can see it only by colour.
steps: Open Work history and click a task.
Find the Task plan section, headed Plan with the step count.
Read the steps and the coloured dot next to each one.
Compare each dot with the step result after the run finishes.
S60.14.where: Command palette (Cmd+K) > Work history > click a task > Task plan section

S60.16.note: The running step has no text label; only its dot colour marks it.
steps: Open Work history and click a task that is still running.
Look at the Task plan section.
Find the step with the filled dot in the running colour.
Wait and check that the marked step moves forward as the run continues.
S60.16.where: Command palette (Cmd+K) > Work history > click a running task > Task plan section

S60.17.needs: a Work task that runs tools in parallel
S60.17.note: Whether the agent runs tools in parallel depends on the task; the group only appears when two or more tools share a parallel group.
steps: Start a Work task that runs several tools at once.
Open the tool activity list in the chat while the task runs.
Look for a group marked with the word parallel and a branch icon.
Compare the grouped tools with what ran at the same time.
S60.17.where: Work chat > tool activity list > group labelled parallel

S60.18.needs: a paid account, a project selected
S60.18.note: The card appears only when the agent decides to ask; the tester cannot force it.
steps: Send a short, vague Work request.
If the agent asks a question, read the card with its options.
Pick an option or type in Something else…, then click Send answers.
Check the agent continues the task with your answer.
S60.18.where: Work chat > clarifying question card (Send answers)

steps: Open Work history and choose the Needs you filter.
Find a task with the card Waiting for your approval.
Read the tool call shown on the card.
Click Approve or Deny, then check the task resumes or stops.
S60.19.where: Tasks (Work history) > Needs you filter > task card: Waiting for your approval > Approve or Deny

labels.text: Message the agent to add instructions or change course

S60.20.needs: a task that is still running
steps: Open Work history and click a running task.
Click into the box Message the agent to add instructions or change course.
Type new guidance and click Send.
Check the queued message appears and the task changes course without restarting.
S60.20.where: Work history > open a running task > Message the agent box > Send

S60.21.note: The step-boundary timing of the pause is not visible in the UI.
steps: Open Work history on a running task.
Click Pause on the task row (List) or card (Board).
Watch the badge change to Pausing and then Paused.
Check that the task keeps its completed steps when it stops.
S60.21.where: Work history > List or Board > task > Pause

steps: Open Work history and choose the Active filter.
Find a task with the badge Paused.
Click Resume on the row or card.
Check the task continues from its last completed step.
S60.22.where: Work history > Active filter > paused task > Resume

S60.23.note: Stop was found on the Board layout only; the List layout was not verified.
steps: Open Work history and click the Board layout.
Find a running task card.
Click Stop on the card.
Check the task ends as Stopped and the run stops on the server.
S60.23.where: Work history > Board > task card > Stop

S60.24.needs: a Work task with a failed step
S60.24.note: Whether the button appears for every failed step was not verified; a failed run is needed to test it.
steps: Run a Work task until a step fails.
Find the plan review card for that run.
Click Retry from this step on the step that failed.
Check the task continues from that step.
S60.24.where: Work chat > plan review card > Retry from this step

S60.25.note: No separate Restart control was found; Re-run this task is the closest match.
steps: Open Work history and click a finished task (not a live one).
Find the Goal block and click Re-run this task.
A new Work chat opens with the goal, constraints and deliverable filled in.
Send it and compare the new run with the old one.
S60.25.where: Work history > click a finished task > Re-run this task

S60.26.note: No Duplicate label was found in the tasks UI (searched TasksPage.tsx, TaskDetailPanel.tsx and the tasks folder). The nearest control is Re-run this task (TaskDetailPanel.tsx), which loads the goal into a new Work chat; desktop DesktopTasks.tsx was not opened.

steps: Open Work history and click a completed task.
Find the section labelled Result.
Read the result text.
Compare it with what the task produced.
S60.29.where: Work history > click a finished task > Result section

S60.30.note: Without files the section says No generated files are recorded for this task.
steps: Open Work history and click a task that produced files.
Open the Outputs section.
Click Download and open on a file.
Check the file opens or downloads and matches the name and size shown.
S60.30.where: Work history > click a task > Outputs section > Download and open

steps: Open Work history and choose the All filter.
Click a task whose state is Partially completed.
Read the line Done X of Y steps before it stopped.
Read the Remaining: list and compare with what was done.
S60.31.where: Work history > Archived or All filter > task with state Partially completed > Task plan section

S60.32.needs: none (more tasks make it easier to test)
steps: Press Cmd+K and choose Work history.
Click each filter: Active, Needs you, All, Archived.
Switch between List and Board.
Click Show more if it appears, then open any task and compare its state with the badge.
S60.32.where: Command palette (Cmd+K) > Work history, or sidebar Chats and tasks > Tasks filter; then Work history filters Active, Needs you, All, Archived

S60.33.needs: a Free or paid account with at least one finished work task that has a source chat
S60.33.note: The share button sends the user to the source chat's share dialog (apps/web/features/tasks/components/TasksPage.tsx:40 uses ?share=true, handled in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:1686), so it shares the conversation, not a separate task view. Whether the plan, steps and results are all included in that share was not verified. The exact dialog title was not confirmed as a task-specific label. Confirmed the dialog exists at apps/web/features/chat/components/share/ShareConversationDialog.tsx.
steps: Sign in and open Work history from the home screen link "Work history" or the command palette.
Click a task that has a source chat and is not live (a finished one), so its details open on the right.
Expand the details section of the task panel.
Click the button "Share task" (it only appears when the task has a source chat and is not running).

Look for the share dialog on the source chat (the app opens /chat/<id>?share=true, which opens the chat's share dialog) and compare with Expected: the task's plan, steps and results should be shareable. Note: the handler shares the source conversation, not a separate task record.
S60.33.where: Work history (route /tasks, also reached from the command palette action or the "Work history" link on the home screen) > open a finished task in the list > open the details panel > expand the details disclosure > Share task

labels.text: Another device already resumed this task.
Another device already answered this approval.

S60.34.needs: a paid account (signed in on two devices) and a running task; a Free account may not have work tasks
S60.34.note: The run list comes from the server (getClient().listRuns in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TasksPage.tsx:247), so the cross-device behaviour depends on the server side. The Expected behaviour was not judged. The web page's list fetch (apps/web/features/tasks/components/TasksPage.tsx) and the list route apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/route.ts were not read beyond the lines named in the plan.
steps: On device A, start a work task and note its title in Work history.
On device B (same account, signed in), open Work history.
Find the same task in the list (the list filter defaults to "active") and click it.
On device B, try a running control such as "Pause", "Cancel", or a pending approval ("Approve" or "Deny").

Compare with Expected: device B should show the same task state as device A and be able to act on it. A message such as "Another device already resumed this task." or "Another device already answered this approval." means the action was refused because device A acted first.
S60.34.where: Work history (route /tasks) > open a task from the list, or open a link with ?run=<id>; the list is loaded from the server, so the same account on another device shows the same tasks
